title: Private parties, medical school, marriage and time for jazz
summary: Steinau had few jam sessions; they place his marriage, finishing medical school in 1952 and the year away, which limited his jazz following.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Did you, uh, did we go to many private parties, or did you go to many private parties? I don't think many others. You mean whether there were musicians? Yeah, whether there were musicians, or a jam session?
Oh, uh, not a lot, because I don't know that there were all that many, but certainly I would think three or four a year maybe, which, and I suspect probably a dozen or so altogether.
Which was certainly a lot more than I ever had before, or since.

Well, of course, let's see, I can't remember what year you got married. I got married in 52. Yeah. And so, uh, you were just about through with medical school. Yeah, I finished in 52. Yeah. And it seems to me you got married in the spring, or? February. February, or the one I'm going to say. Anyway, but just before...
And then I was out of town.
Yeah, and you were out of town.
From, uh, from July of 52 through June of 53.
Well, you had plenty of time to, uh, and, and, and, I won't say you had plenty of time, you had more time before you were married, and had those responsibilities, and...

I don't know for sure. Yeah. I was, I was in school, or I was, and the summers I was out of town working a good part of the time. Uh, no, I didn't really have large quantities of time to follow around.
Yeah, well, certainly after, after children comes, that ties you down, too. I see. Yeah.
Because, uh, I'm just thinking about parties I went to and things, and I can't remember how many of Herbert Otto's parties you went to.
